stories.title: This Maryland startup wants to take the anxiety out of auto care — and prove your mechanic isn't ripping you off
stories.summary: Moving to Maryland showed Precious Jones how inconsistent car repair prices can be. So she built FairRide AI, a platform that grades mechanic estimates with a fairness score against local market rates. It's already helping 200 users — and won her $6,000 from Wells Fargo.
stories.extended_summary: After relocating to Maryland, Precious Jones noticed something unsettling: car repair estimates seemed to have no rhyme or reason. So she created FairRide AI, a platform that evaluates mechanic quotes with a fairness score from 1 to 100 based on local market rates. Users just upload their estimate and get an itemized breakdown showing typical price ranges for each service. Built with the Base44 vibecoding platform, the tool is already serving around 200 users. Jones took second place at the Greater Baltimore Urban League's pitch competition and won $6,000 from Wells Fargo — and she's now partnering with local mechanics to sharpen labor-cost accuracy. Her message: knowledge is power when it comes to auto care.

Since her days as a public defender in Utah, Noella Sudbury has been obsessed with solving a problem: How do you help someone with a criminal record get a job? Bottom line: It's really hard.
